message.content:
I need a concrete, staged implementation plan for the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma VPS-hosting platform). Three deep research agents just audited the entire codebase for "single-node assumption" bugs now that the platform has grown from one Proxmox compute node (primary, OVH Singapore) to two (node-2, Hetzner Falkenstein, just onboarded today). Their findings are synthesized below — this is COMPLETE, VERIFIED research (file:line citations already confirmed), not speculation. Your job is to design the implementation plan, not to re-research.

## Ground truth already confirmed

**Architecture**: `Node` Prisma model (schema.prisma) holds one row per physical Proxmox host: `apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret` (Proxmox API creds — already correctly used everywhere for VM-level operations via `pveFor()`/`pveForNode()` in lib/proxmox.ts), `publicIp`, `natChain`, `bridge`, `subnetPrefix`, `provider` (OVH/HETZNER enum), `region`. `Server.nodeId` links a server to its node. There is exactly ONE worker process for the whole platform (`worker/index.ts`, one systemd unit `nxeon-worker`, runs only on the primary machine) — confirmed via package.json, CLAUDE.md, and scripts/onboard-node.sh's own header comment which explicitly states each node is a separate NAT island with no cross-node private networking, and the worker's NAT chain "only manages forwards local to the host it runs on."

**Bug Class A — one shared root-cause function, fixable with pure code (no new infra)**:
`lib/sftp.ts`'s `connectionTarget()` (~line 137-143) and the `SftpServer` type (~line 35-41) it operates on: for any server WITHOUT a dedicated IP, it resolves the SSH host as `process.env.PUBLIC_IP` (a single global env var = the primary's IP), NEVER consulting `server.nodeId`/`server.node.publicIp`. This function is the shared foundation for `lib/ssh-exec.ts`'s `withServerSsh()`/`exec()` and `lib/sftp.ts`'s `withSftp()`, which together are the SSH plumbing for nearly the entire customer control panel. Two places already do this correctly and prove the fix pattern: `worker/index.ts:712,814` compute `server.node?.publicIp ?? process.env.PUBLIC_IP` inline; `worker/game-subdomain-sync.ts`'s `resolveGameServerDnsTarget()` prefers `input.nodePublicIp` correctly.

Confirmed downstream-affected files (all call `withServerSsh`/`withSftp`/`connectionTarget` and need `node: { select: { publicIp: true } }` threaded into their Prisma query, once the shared function itself is fixed): `terminal-server/index.ts` (web SSH terminal), `lib/actions-game-control.ts` (customer game console/RCON/kick/ban/backups), `worker/game-control.ts` (game power/backup/scheduled-restart/player-tracking sweeps — these fire every ~60s), `worker/websites.ts`, `worker/databases.ts`, `worker/services.ts`, `worker/site-publish.ts`, `worker/apps.ts` (cPanel-lite control panel), `worker/ssl.ts` (certbot issuance), `worker/volumes.ts` (guest-side format/mount only — Proxmox-side already correct), `worker/disk-expand.ts` (guest-side growpart/resize2fs only — Proxmox-side already correct), `worker/game-mods.ts` (currently behind `ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS` flag, off by default), `worker/game-config.ts`, `worker/migrate-real.ts`'s `connectTarget()` (destination-VM side of migrations only), `worker/ssh-health.ts` (a fleet-wide sweep — currently WILL false-alarm every ~15min for any node-2 server), `lib/claude-backfill.ts`/`scripts/backfill-claude.ts`, `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`'s `freemcHost()` (lower urgency, currently masked because that one Server row happens to lack a dedicated IP so it's not exercised yet... actually re-check: it has NO dedicated IP either per live DB check, so this is exercised — but it currently lives ON the primary so it's not broken YET, only if freemc-host is ever moved to a non-primary node).

Three files bypass `connectionTarget` entirely with an even more broken pattern — direct dial to the guest's PRIVATE `10.20.x.x` IP (works only because today everything is on one node's bridge): `worker/claude.ts:85-104` (AI build feature), `worker/game-update.ts:104-119` (6-hourly game auto-update sweep), `worker/firewall.ts:95-107` (per-server firewall sync job). These should be rewritten to route through the same (once-fixed) `connectionTarget`/`withServerSsh` path — turning them into Bug-Class-A fixes too, rather than needing new network infrastructure.

**Bug Class B — genuinely needs new infrastructure (the worker has no OS-level access to a second physical node)**:
1. `worker/network.ts`'s `syncPortForwards()`/`reconcileNatChain()` — rebuilds NAT/DNAT iptables rules via local `execFile("iptables",...)`, always on whatever machine the worker itself runs on (primary). A NAT-based (non-dedicated-IP) server on node-2 can never get a working port-forward from this code as written. This is the original bug that triggered this whole audit (tracked internally as "P1-18").
2. `worker/index.ts`'s `provision()` step writes the per-VM cloud-init vendor snippet via plain Node.js `fs.writeFile()` to a local path (`SNIPPET_DIR`), referenced via a global `SNIPPET_STORAGE` env var — for a VM provisioned on node-2, Proxmox on node-2 is told to read a snippet file that was only ever written to the PRIMARY's disk. Result: the VM boots and reports "ready" but the game/app install script, Claude Code, telemetry shipper, and security hardening never actually run — a silently-broken, empty server that looks fine in the UI.
3. `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`'s `hasLiveDnatRule()` — checks for an existing DNAT rule via local `execFile("iptables", ["-t","nat","-S","PREROUTING"])` before allocating a dedicated IP, to avoid double-allocating. For a node-2 IP, this checks the WRONG host's (primary's) iptables — a real "hand an internally-used IP to a customer" risk.

Because these all fundamentally need to read/write OS-level state (iptables rules, local files) on a DIFFERENT physical machine than the one Next.js/the worker process runs on, and the codebase's established security posture is "Proxmox hosts are managed purely via a scoped, token-authenticated API — never direct root SSH" (this is a deliberate existing convention, confirmed by the `Node` model having NO ssh fields, only apiUrl/tokenId/tokenSecret, unlike the separate `HostingNode` model which DOES have ssh fields for a different, already-correctly-multi-node-safe product), the user has explicitly said they want "the primary node to have complete control of all nodes, complete sync" and asked for a plan to build that — meaning a SSH-to-node approach would be a deliberate, known departure from that existing convention, whereas a small SCOPED per-node agent (analogous to how each node already has its own Proxmox API token) would preserve it. I need you to design this — evaluate both options concretely (a lightweight per-node HTTP agent/service vs. SSH-based remote-exec from the worker) and recommend one, considering: security posture consistency with the existing Proxmox-API-token pattern, implementation complexity, and how it generalizes to node #3/#4/etc. Whichever is chosen needs: how the primary calls it, how auth works (token pattern matching `Node.tokenId`/`tokenSecret`?), what operations it exposes (at minimum: sync NAT/DNAT rules from a declarative ruleset, write a snippet file to local storage, query local iptables NAT rules), and how `scripts/onboard-node.sh` would need to change to install/register it on new nodes.

**Other confirmed, separate bugs found** (need their own fix, not part of Class A/B):
- `lib/monitoring.ts`'s `backupSummary()` merges every node's backup listing into one combined `{count, newestCtime, oldestCtime}` before staleness-checking — a healthy node-1 backup masks a silently-broken node-2 backup schedule forever. Needs per-node staleness signals instead of one merged scalar.
- `lib/platform-backups.ts` (powers the admin disaster-recovery panel) reads ONLY local files (`/tank/backup/status`, `/tank/backup/platform`) on whichever box the web app happens to run on — zero awareness that a second node's data even exists. Contrast: the SAME admin page's customer-backup section already correctly loops nodes and shows an honesty banner when some can't be enumerated (`app/admin/backups/logic.ts`/`page.tsx` — use as the reference pattern).
- `app/api/servers/[id]/backups/download/route.ts` correctly checks tenancy via the per-node Proxmox API, but then reads the actual `.vma.zst` file bytes via `fs.stat`/`createReadStream` from a LOCAL path derived from the legacy singleton `pve` client (`lib/proxmox.ts`'s `backupDumpDir()`) — will 502 "not available on the host" for every node-2 server's backup download, since the file physically lives on node-2's disk, not the primary's.
- **Live security exposure, separate and more urgent than the rest**: `scripts/onboard-node.sh` never installs any firewall hardening (no `nxeon-firewall.service`, no `/etc/nxeon/admin-ips.nft` allowlist) on a new node — and no such systemd-unit template even exists in the repo to copy (checked `deploy/`, found only backup-family units). Node-2 was onboarded today and almost certainly currently has NO admin-IP-allowlist restricting SSH (port 22) or the Proxmox web UI (port 8006) — wide open to the whole internet. This needs an urgent, mostly-manual/scripted remediation, separate from the rest of this architectural plan (should happen first, fast, not bundled into a multi-week build).
- At least one `Server` row (`minecraft-mm8w85`, confirmed via QA-PRELAUNCH.md) has `nodeId: null`. Given `worker/index.ts`'s/`worker/volumes.ts`'s/`worker/disk-expand.ts`'s `nodeFor()` fallback-to-primary pattern, and `lib/proxmox.ts`'s legacy `listBackups()`/`listSnapshots()` singleton calls (used when `server.node` is null), any such row is now a real vmid-collision risk for cross-tenant backup/snapshot exposure now that a second node exists. This is a simple, safe one-time data-hygiene fix: backfill `nodeId` to the primary's id for every `Server` row where it's currently null and the server is confirmed to actually be running on the primary (which today, all of them are).
- No template/OS-image sync or drift-verification between nodes exists (`OsTemplate.vmid` is a bare global integer with no per-node mapping) — lower priority; already partially/manually handled once today via vzdump/qmrestore for node-2's initial 5 templates, but nothing prevents future drift or verifies parity.

## Your task

Design a concrete, staged implementation plan covering:
1. **The node-agent architecture decision** (Class B fixes) — recommend a specific design (endpoints, auth, deployment) and justify it against the SSH alternative.
2. **The Class A fix** — the exact shape of the `lib/sftp.ts`/`SftpServer`/`connectionTarget()` change, and a sensible grouping/ordering for threading `node` through the ~20 confirmed call sites (which ones matter most, which can be batched).
3. **The 3 direct-private-IP-dial rewrites** (claude.ts, game-update.ts, firewall.ts) — confirm these fold cleanly into the Class A fix.
4. **The separate bugs** (backup staleness merging, platform-backups local-only view, backup-download 502, dedicated-ip double-check, nodeId:null backfill) — where each fits in sequencing.
5. **The urgent firewall gap** — what the immediate remediation looks like (likely: extend onboard-node.sh + a reusable firewall-install step, and confirm/apply it to node-2 right now as an out-of-band urgent action, separate from the staged rollout).
6. **Sequencing/phasing** — what must happen before what, and what can be parallelized. Identify the critical files for each phase.
7. **Verification strategy** for each phase — how to confirm each fix actually works (given there are currently zero real customers on node-2, so this can be tested safely).

Also design what should go into TWO documentation deliverables the user explicitly asked for (do not write them yet, just specify their scope/outline as part of the plan): (a) a permanent "how multi-node synergy works + how to add node N" reference doc for future node onboarding, and (b) a retrospective/summary doc of the multi-node rollout + Hetzner node-2 onboarding work already completed (schema, admin UI, dashboards, the QEMU rescue-mode install saga and its two real gotchas, template migration) — this second one already has a start at docs/DOCUMENTATION.md (search for "Onboarding a Hetzner dedicated node via rescue-mode QEMU install" to see what's already there) but the user wants a more complete treatment covering the WHOLE multi-node effort, not just the physical install gotchas.

Produce a clear, well-organized, prioritized implementation plan. Do not write or edit any actual application files — this is planning only. Be concrete about file paths and function names using the citations already given above; you don't need to re-verify them, just build the plan on top of them.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Nxeon — onboard a fresh Proxmox VE host as a compute node
# =============================================================================
# Run this ON the new Proxmox host (as root). It idempotently preps everything a
# Nxeon compute node needs, then prints the exact values to paste into the admin
# "Add node" form (/admin/nodes/new). Re-running is safe: every step checks
# current state before changing anything.
#
# What it does:
#   1. Create a NAT bridge vmbrX bound to a per-node /24 (e.g. 10.20.N.1/24)
#   2. Enable IPv4 forwarding + a MASQUERADE rule for that subnet (append-only)
#   3. Create the NVMe + HDD storages matching the Node's storageNvme/storageHdd
#   4. Create the cloud-init snippets dir + the nxeon vendor snippet
#   5. Create a Proxmox API role + user + token with the privileges the platform
#      needs (documented pveum commands)
#   6. Build (or document copying) the cloud-init templates VMID 9000-9004
#   7. Print the Add-node form values (apiUrl, tokenId, tokenSecret, pveNode,
#      subnetPrefix, natChain, sshPort range, storages, publicIp)
#
# SAFETY:

type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop;

        # Keep this rule FIRST. It is what lets an already-established SSH

        # ICMP (ping, path MTU discovery) — keep it working. Path MTU black

        # Customer VMs (vmbr1) must NOT reach host services — they route
        # outbound via the forward chain and use public DNS, so drop VM->host
        # input entirely. THREAT: a compromised tenant VM pivoting from its
        # own guest into the hypervisor's SSH, Proxmox API or Postgres.
        # This rule sits ABOVE the admin allowlist on purpose: a tenant VM
        # must not gain admin reachability by spoofing an allowlisted source.
        # (Allow only DNS to the gateway if a future setup needs it.)
        #
        # EXCEPTION (2026-08-23): nxeon.cloud itself (the public website) runs
        # on THIS host, not in a VM, so any VM resolving nxeon.cloud's public
        # DNS name hairpins straight back into this same INPUT chain — it is
        # not "some other external site" reached via the forward chain, it IS
        # this host. That is not the threat this rule guards against (SSH /
        # Proxmox API / Postgres); it broke a legitimate case — Kodely (VM 110)
        # calling the Nxeon partner API like any ordinary HTTPS client — with
        # no security benefit, since 80/443 are already open to the entire
        # public internet two rules below regardless of source. Narrow carve-
        # out for exactly those two ports; every other host port stays fully
        # blocked from vmbr1.
        iifname "vmbr1" tcp dport { 80, 443 } accept
        iifname "vmbr1" drop

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES — allowlisted sources only
        #   tcp/22    host root SSH

        # Two rules because in the `inet` family an `ip saddr` match only ever
        # matches IPv4 packets and an `ip6 saddr` match only ever matches IPv6
        # packets. Omitting the v6 rule would not "leave IPv6 alone" — it
        # would deny it via policy drop. The counters make it obvious after
        # the fact which family you actually connected over

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        ip  saddr @nxeon_admin_v4 tcp dport $ADMIN_PORTS counter accept
        ip6 saddr @nxeon_admin_v6 tcp dport $ADMIN_PORTS counter accept

        # Everything else aimed at the admin ports is denied. Logged at a hard

7235	## Onboarding a Hetzner dedicated node via rescue-mode QEMU install (2026-09-05)
7236	
7237	Nxeon's second compute node (`node-2`, Hetzner auction server #3068915, Falkenstein, `nxeon-fsn1`,
7238	178.63.94.114) was onboarded using the standard "install via QEMU inside Hetzner's rescue system"
7239	technique: boot into Hetzner rescue, download the official Proxmox VE ISO, bake an automated-install
7240	`answer.toml` into it with `proxmox-auto-install-assistant`, then boot that ISO under
7241	`qemu-system-x86_64` with the real physical disks passed through directly (`-drive file=/dev/nvme0n1`
7242	etc., emulated as `-device nvme` so the guest sees the same `nvme0n1`/`nvme1n1` names the answer file's
7243	`disk-list` references), so the installer partitions the actual hardware. When it finishes, reboot the
7244	physical host out of rescue mode into the fresh install.
7245	
7246	**Real gotcha #1 — the network `filter` must match the EMULATED NIC, not the real one.** The
7247	automated installer's `[network]` answer-file section needs a `filter.ID_NET_NAME_MAC` (or similar) to
7248	pick which NIC to configure. It's tempting to set this to the REAL hardware NIC's MAC (read via
7249	`udevadm info -p /sys/class/net/eth0` in rescue mode beforehand) — but during the QEMU install, the
7250	installer only ever sees QEMU's *emulated* NIC, which has a different MAC unless you explicitly spoof
7251	it. Fix: pass `-netdev user,id=net0 -device virtio-net-pci,netdev=net0,mac=<real-nic-mac>` to `qemu`
7252	so the emulated NIC's MAC matches what the answer file's filter expects. Without this the installer
7253	aborts cleanly with `ERROR: Installation failed: filter did not match any device` — annoying but safe
7254	(no partial install).
7255	
7256	**Real gotcha #2 — the real hang: the emulated NIC's INTERFACE NAME leaks into `/etc/network/interfaces`.**
7257	Even after fixing gotcha #1, the resulting install boots to a *completely silent* host — no ping, no
7258	SSH, indefinitely — which looks exactly like a hung/crashed boot. It is not. The installer's network
7259	setup writes the interface name it saw for the matched NIC *at install time* into
7260	`/etc/network/interfaces` (e.g. `auto vmbr0 ... bridge-ports ens5`). Under QEMU, a `virtio-net-pci`
7261	device gets a PCI-Express slot-based name like `ens5` — a name that has nothing to do with the real
7262	hardware's PCI topology. On the real physical box, the same NIC gets whatever systemd-udevd's
7263	predictable-naming scheme actually assigns (onboard index like `eno1` takes priority when the
7264	firmware provides `ID_NET_NAME_ONBOARD`, which `udevadm info` will show ahead of time). Since `ens5`
7265	never exists on the real hardware, the bridge never comes up, and the OS boots completely fine with a
7266	dead network — indistinguishable from a boot hang from the outside.
7267	
7268	**Fix, done live via a follow-up rescue-mode session:** reboot into rescue, `apt-get install
7269	zfs-fuse` (this rescue kernel's exact build doesn't have a matching `zfs-dkms` target — `zfs-fuse` is
7270	a userspace ZFS impl that doesn't care) OR use Hetzner's own `/usr/local/sbin/zpool` wrapper, which
7271	offers to compile OpenZFS from source against the *exact* running rescue kernel (works, takes ~1-2
7272	min, answer `y` to the CDDL/GPL notice) — either way, `zpool import -N -f -R /mnt rpool`, `zfs mount`
7273	the root + data datasets, edit `/etc/network/interfaces` to replace the QEMU-era interface name with
7274	the real one, `zpool export rpool`, reboot. Confirmed the real interface name ahead of time via
7275	`udevadm info -p /sys/class/net/<ifname>` while still in the FIRST rescue session (`ID_NET_NAME_ONBOARD`)
7276	so the fix wasn't a guess.
7277	
7278	**Lesson for next time:** decide the real interface name from `udevadm` BEFORE running the automated
7279	install, and consider setting the answer file's network filter AND expected interface name to
7280	whatever the real hardware will assign — or simplest, just always plan for this one manual
7281	`/etc/network/interfaces` edit as a normal step of this onboarding method, not an exceptional failure.
7282	Silence (no ping, no SSH) after a QEMU-installed reboot is NOT necessarily a firmware/boot-order
7283	problem — check the installed system's actual network config from rescue mode before assuming
7284	anything about the boot process itself. (A red herring chased first: BIOS boot-order priority hitting
7285	a blank spare disk before the OS disks — real hardware here does default to legacy BIOS, confirmed via
7286	`[ -d /sys/firmware/efi ]` in rescue mode, and cloning the NVMe mirror's GRUB boot code onto the blank
7287	SATA SSD via `dd` was a reasonable, low-risk thing to try, but it was not the actual cause.)
7288	
7289	**Template parity:** rather than building fresh cloud-init templates (9000-9004) on the new node,
7290	`vzdump <id> --dumpdir /tank/backup` on the primary for each, `scp` the `.vma` files to the new node's
7291	own `/tank/backup`, then `qmrestore <file> <id> --storage vmdata` — `qmrestore` preserves the
7292	`template: 1` flag from the original config automatically (the "you can't convert a template to a
7293	template" message on a subsequent `qm template <id>` call is expected/harmless, not an error). This
7294	keeps every node's base images byte-identical, matching `scripts/onboard-node.sh`'s own stated
7295	preference over `--build-templates`.
7296

That turns "build firewall hardening" into "port a proven system," which is materially faster and lower-risk than building one from scratch. Details below.

I also found several things that make the rollout cheaper than the raw file count suggests: `worker/volumes.ts` and `worker/disk-expand.ts` **already select the full `node` relation** (they needed it for `pveFor()`), so they'll self-heal the moment the root `connectionTarget()` fix lands — zero code change required. ## 1. Node-agent architecture decision (Class B)

**Recommendation: a lightweight per-node HTTP agent with its own bearer token, not SSH.**

### Why, concretely

- **Consistency with the existing security posture.** `Node` (prisma/schema.prisma:1151) deliberately has no SSH fields — only `apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret`. Every Proxmox-node interaction already goes through a scoped, token-authenticated API client (`pveFor`/`pveForNode`, lib/proxmox.ts:87-126), never raw root shell. `HostingNode` (schema.prisma:1432) is the one place SSH-to-a-remote-box exists in this codebase, and it's a deliberately different product with a different trust model (`sshHost`/`sshPort`/`rootPasswordEnc`, hardened via `onboard-hosting-node.sh` run *over that SSH connection*). Introducing worker→Proxmox-host SSH for `Node` would quietly merge two trust models the schema currently keeps apart. An HTTP agent with its own scoped token preserves the invariant "every physical host is reached via a narrow, token-authenticated API" platform-wide.
- **Blast radius.** SSH grants an arbitrary root shell. The agent's entire surface is 4-6 named, typed operations (sync one NAT rule, write one snippet file under one directory, read local NAT rows, stream one backup file). A leaked/misused agent token can't do anything the code doesn't explicitly expose; a leaked SSH credential can do anything. It also avoids re-litigating the shell-injection-allowlist discipline `lib/ssh-exec.ts` and `worker/migrate-real.ts` carry (DOMAIN_RE/IDENT_RE/PATH_RE/etc., "reject — never sanitize") a second time for platform-internal calls that don't need a general shell at all.
- **The integration point already exists and is already tested.** `lib/nat-rules.ts`'s `NatHost` type (line 276-283: `ensureChain`, `listChain`, `addRule`, `deleteRule`) is the exact seam `worker/network.ts`'s `iptablesHost()` implements today, built specifically so `reconcileNatChain`'s H5-incident-driven diff/apply/read-back-and-prove logic (lib/nat-rules.ts:307-362) could be tested against an in-memory fake (test/nat-sync.test.ts) with no kernel, no root, no network. An HTTP-backed `NatHost` implementation slots in with **zero changes to the tested reconciliation logic** — only a new transport for 4 primitives. This is the strongest concrete argument for the HTTP-agent design: the hardest part of Class B needs no redesign at all.
- **Generalizes to node #3/#4.** Onboarding already mints a node-specific Proxmox token (`onboard-node.sh` step 5: "Create a Proxmox API role + user + token"). Minting a second, purpose-built token and installing one small systemd service is one more structurally identical step in the same script — not a new credential-lifecycle paradigm (host keys, known_hosts, root-login policy) running in parallel with the existing one.
- **Auth pattern.** Reuse the *shape* of `Node.tokenId`/`tokenSecret` (primary calls the node with a bearer credential) but mint a **separate** credential rather than reusing the Proxmox token — precedented exactly by `lib/telemetry-token.ts`'s `mintTelemetryToken()`/`hashTelemetryToken()` (random 32-byte token, SHA-256 hash stored on the row, raw value shown once). Add `Node.agentTokenHash String?` to the schema; the agent itself just holds the one raw token in a 0600 file (`/etc/nxeon/node-agent-token`) and does a constant-time compare — it doesn't need a lookup-by-hash table the way multi-tenant `Server.telemetryTokenHash` does.

### Concrete design

- **New service**: `node-agent/index.ts` (parallel to `terminal-server/`, `worker/`), a small tsx/Node HTTP(S) server. New unit `deploy/nxeon-node-agent.service` (finally giving `deploy/` the template it's missing) → `nxeon-node-agent.service` on each non-primary node.
- **The primary does not run the agent.** Add a dispatch helper, e.g. `natHostFor(node)` in `worker/network.ts`, that returns the existing local `iptablesHost()` when `node === null || node.isPrimary`, else an `agentNatHost(node)` HTTP adapter. Same pattern for the snippet-write and dedicated-IP check call sites. This avoids adding a moving part (and a firewall hole) to the primary for no benefit.
- **Endpoints** (JSON, bearer auth via `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, one primitive per NatHost method rather than a chunky "sync" endpoint — keeps 100% of the tested decision logic on the primary):
  - `GET /v1/health` — liveness/version; used by `testNode()` (lib/actions-nodes.ts:246) and a periodic reachability sweep.
  - `POST /v1/nat/ensure-chain` `{chain}` → mirrors `ensureChain()` (worker/network.ts:22-51).
  - `GET /v1/nat/chain/:chain` → raw `iptables -t nat -S <chain>` stdout, mirrors `listChain()`.
  - `POST /v1/nat/rule` / `DELETE /v1/nat/rule` `{chain, rule: NatRule}` → mirrors `addRule`/`deleteRule`, reusing `NatRule`/`ruleSpec` from lib/nat-rules.ts verbatim.
  - `POST /v1/snippet` `{filename, content}` (filename allowlisted to `nxeon-<vmid>.yaml`) and `DELETE /v1/snippet/:filename` → fixes Class B #2 (worker/index.ts:616, :915).
  - `GET /v1/iptables/dnat-check?address=X` → mirrors `hasLiveDnatRule()`'s exact query (lib/dedicated-ip.ts:22-33) → fixes Class B #3.
  - Phase-3 extension (not day one): `GET /v1/backup/:filename` (stream bytes, reusing the same `ARCHIVE_RE` + basename-confinement checks already in the download route) and `GET /v1/backup-status` (mirrors `readPlatformBackups()`'s local reads) — these directly fix the backup-download 502 and the platform-backups blind spot using the *same* infrastructure, rather than inventing separate mechanisms for them.
- **Network exposure**: agent binds to the node's public IP on its own port, gated by that node's own nftables to accept **only the primary's public IP** (a single-source allow rule using the exact mechanism `admin-ip.sh`/`firewall.nft` already implement for tcp/8006 — a new set, not the human admin allowlist). A WireGuard/VXLAN mesh (already flagged as a deliberate future follow-up in `onboard-node.sh`'s header) would be a strictly better transport later, but isn't required to ship this correctly now.
- **Admin UI**: extend `/admin/nodes/new` and `addNode()`/`updateNode()` (lib/actions-nodes.ts:160-211) with an `agentToken` field — the raw value pasted from onboarding is hashed immediately server-side and only the hash is stored, never redisplayed. Extend `testNode()` (lib/actions-nodes.ts:246) to also probe `GET /v1/health`.
- **onboard-node.sh changes**: add a new numbered step that (a) ships a single bundled JS file for the agent (via `tsc`/`esbuild` — avoid requiring a full monorepo checkout + `npm install` on a bare Proxmox host), (b) generates the token and writes it 0600, (c) installs+enables `nxeon-node-agent.service` from the new `deploy/` template, (d) adds the primary's IP to that node's agent-port allowlist, (e) prints the token into the same "Add node" form block the script already prints at the end (mirrors how it prints the Proxmox `Token secret` today).

## 2. Class A fix — shape and call-site rollout

### The fix itself (lib/sftp.ts)

```ts
export type SftpServer = {
  id: string;
  rootPassword: string | null;
  rootPasswordEnc?: string | null;
  sshPort: number | null;
  dedicatedIp?: { address: string } | null;
  node?: { publicIp: string } | null;   // NEW — optional/nullable
};

export function connectionTarget(server: SftpServer): { host: string; port: number } | null {
  const dedicated = !!server.dedicatedIp;
  const host = dedicated
    ? server.dedicatedIp!.address
    : (server.node?.publicIp ?? process.env.PUBLIC_IP ?? "");
  const port = dedicated ? 22 : server.sshPort;
  if (!host || !port) return null;
  return { host, port };
}
```

`node` stays **optional**, not required, for two reasons: (1) it preserves today's exact behavior — falling back to `process.env.PUBLIC_IP` — for the one legitimate `nodeId: null` edge case (once the backfill below runs, that fallback increasingly means "no node = true legacy," not "somebody forgot to select it"); (2) it lets the ~18 downstream files be migrated one at a time, each individually verifiable, rather than a single atomic multi-file commit.

This is the entire root-cause fix — a 4-line function + 1-line type addition. Everything below inherits it automatically once each file's query selects `node`.
